_about: Known differences between the Node codec and testdata/bson-vectors/v1.json, re-derived against this codec (the five ported fixes included). Each entry: verdict (deliberate: a documented refusal or residual of this driver; acceptable: the same value in another form, or accepted by the server and the owner), what Node does, what the corpus says, the reason. test/unit/bson-corpus.test.ts reads this file, skips nothing, fails on any vector not listed here, and fails on an entry whose vector now agrees.

datetime/int64-max.node: the Extended JSON writer (the only way to write a type the driver has no value for) builds an Invalid Date and writes int64 0
datetime/int64-max.reason: a datetime beyond the Date range is refused on read and an Invalid Date is refused on write, so the driver never writes the epoch in its place

datetime/int64-min.node: the writer builds an Invalid Date and writes int64 0

undefined/undefined.node: the writer turns {"$undefined": true} into a null (type 0a, 080000000a610000)
undefined/undefined.reason: the driver refuses a BSON undefined on read (UnreadableValueError) and has no JavaScript value that writes one

dbpointer/typical.node: the writer turns $dbPointer into an embedded document {$ref, $id, $db} (type 03, 57 bytes)
dbpointer/typical.reason: a genuine dbPointer is refused on read (UnreadableValueError); the driver cannot write one

document/every-type.reason: the document holds an undefined and a dbPointer element, both listed above

datetime/int64-max.corpus: the bytes read and written back unchanged
datetime/int64-max.reason: a datetime beyond the JavaScript Date range (8.64e15 ms either way) has no Date: the driver refuses to read it (UnreadableValueError) rather than build an Invalid Date and write int64 0 in its place

datetime/int64-min.corpus: the bytes read and written back unchanged
datetime/int64-min.reason: a datetime beyond the JavaScript Date range (8.64e15 ms either way) has no Date: the driver refuses to read it (UnreadableValueError) rather than build an Invalid Date and write int64 0 in its place

symbol/typical.node: a symbol (type 0e) reads as a JavaScript string and is written back as a string (type 02)
symbol/typical.reason: README, BSON values: a symbol is deprecated in BSON, the value is kept, only its type byte changes

undefined/undefined.corpus: the bytes read and written back unchanged
undefined/undefined.reason: refused rather than read as JavaScript undefined and dropped on write

dbpointer/typical.corpus: the bytes read and written back unchanged
dbpointer/typical.reason: a dbPointer reads as an embedded document the driver cannot tell from a real one by value, so it is refused rather than written back as another type

array/mixed.node: the double 3.0 reads as the number 3 and is written back as an int32 (61 bytes, 65 expected)
array/mixed.reason: README, BSON values: JavaScript has one number type; the value is unchanged, only int32 or double differs

document/every-type.node: refused on read at the undefined element
document/every-type.corpus: the bytes read and written back unchanged
document/every-type.reason: holds an undefined (see undefined/undefined) and a dbPointer (see dbpointer/typical)

decode/duplicate-keys.node: the decoded values (a: 3, b: 2) write back as 19 bytes
decode/duplicate-keys.corpus: 26 bytes with the key a twice (reencodes_identically is true for an ordered decoder)
decode/duplicate-keys.reason: a JavaScript object cannot hold a repeated key; the last value wins, as the corpus says a mapping decoder must do

decode/regex-options-unsorted.node: the regex options "xi" read, and are written back, as "ix"
decode/regex-options-unsorted.reason: the library stores regex options sorted; the pattern and the set of options are unchanged

reject/key-invalid-utf8.node: the key holding 0xff is read (as U+FFFD); only a string value is UTF-8 checked
reject/key-invalid-utf8.reason: invalid UTF-8 is accepted for the first release (the server accepts it too); a UTF-8 check is a post-release item; this replay fails if the Node codec starts refusing it
